A Right to Test · Executed evidence

What leaves a hidden coding evaluation?

The same fixture coding task and the same attacker, through a naive status-publishing design and ARTT's scheduled release. Status is suppressed for this attack. Score leakage remains noisy, bounded, logged and capped.

Fixture agent, not a real modelSingle call per admissionTrusted custodianSoftware sandbox, not hardware

The public task corpus has 48 tiny Python functions. A custodian-private test context carries a balanced, privately shuffled canary comment, echoed by a deterministic fixture backend. Trial ground truth is never saved in public ledgers. Source code is published for reproducibility.

What the hash chain catches

A hash chain alone cannot detect a deleted tail. A retained checkpoint detects this copy's tail deletion. CT-style witnessing is future work.

The saved checkpoint commits to the original batch head and row count. A holder must keep it independently; it is not a hardware quote or an external witness.

A proposed passport mapping

PROPOSED MAPPING. Not an AIUC or Lucid format; no endorsement or compatibility implied.

One entry per scheduled record carries model and evaluation commitments, the released verdict, privacy charge and ledger provenance. Refusals have no released verdict and cost no additional release epsilon.
